WHY IT HAS TO EXIST

The guards forgot
whose side they're on.

Consumer security is a strange market: you hand total visibility of your digital life to a company, and trust that it guards you instead of monetising you. The record of the last few years says that trust was misplaced.

F·01

The guard sold the house keys

An antivirus vendor spent years collecting its users' browsing data and selling it to over a hundred third parties through a subsidiary, until the US FTC banned the practice and ordered a $16.5 million payment, calling it bait-and-switch surveillance. The product sold as privacy protection was the surveillance.

F·02

The subscription is the product

Year one is cheap; the auto-renewal often costs more than double, buried in the small print. It took the UK competition authority to force the biggest suite vendors to refund customers trapped by auto-renewal. Security priced as a ratchet is rent-seeking with a padlock icon.

F·03

Your safety is their telemetry

A modern suite is a cloud agent with root on your machine; some upload suspicious files and browsing domains with no complete opt-out. Governments have acted on this fear: the US banned a major antivirus outright over what its telemetry could see. The exposure comes from the architecture, so any cloud suite carries it.

F·04

Protection stops at the laptop

The household of 2026 is a network: router, phones, cameras, TVs, NAS, a dozen quiet devices with firmware no one watches. Traditional suites guard one computer and leave the estate open. They cannot see the rogue box on your Wi-Fi until it reaches the PC.

EVERY ALERT CARRIES EVIDENCE. AGENTS WATCH, THEY NEVER TOUCH

WHAT IT CHANGES

From "trust us"
to "check the trace."

The incumbents ask you to trust them. Guardian Shield ships the evidence. Files never leave your device, verifiable by packet trace. Vault plaintext is never on the wire, verifiable by canary-string trace. Two operators in different EU jurisdictions Ed25519-sign every signature update and record it in a public Merkle transparency log. Reproducible builds let anyone byte-diff our binary against source. These are ten reproducible checks you can run yourself.

Files never leave the device.

Local ClamAV + YARA scanning. Signatures come to you; your files never go the other way. Verifiable by tshark, Check 1 of the audit checklist.

Vault plaintext never on the wire.

Argon2id + XChaCha20-Poly1305 client-side. The server sees encrypted opaque blobs. If we could read your passwords, we could hand them over. We can't. Check 2.

Every update signed twice, in public.

Ed25519 threshold: two operators, different jurisdictions, physical Yubikey touch each. Then a 15-minute inspection window. Then a public Merkle-tree entry. Checks 3–5.

THE MECHANICS

Five subsystems,
one honest trust model.

R·01 ships five subsystems; everything else is backlogged. Each subsystem uses well-studied open primitives (ClamAV, YARA, WireGuard-Go, HIBP, OpenPhish, age, Argon2): no proprietary black boxes, no commercial threat-intel SDKs, no third-party analytics on any code path that touches user data. Every other VF product also depends on Guardian Shield for its own defence: the vault primitive that seals VF Wallet, VF Legacy, VF Home + VF Mail; the DNS filter that runs on every VF machine; the scanner that verifies our own signed binaries. See the live security audit ▸

SUBSYSTEM 1

Password vault

Argon2id-wrapped XChaCha20-Poly1305 vault. Autofill on iOS, Android and desktop browsers. Cross-device sync via sealed opaque blobs; we never see the plaintext. Recovery via existing-device confirmation, 24-word recovery code, or a 30-day grace-delay window. Master-password loss is unrecoverable by design.

SUBSYSTEM 2

Malware scanner

ClamAV + YARA, both local, both sandboxed. Signatures updated via daily Ed25519-signed packs published through a public Merkle-tree transparency log. Files never leave the device. Detection floor set at 85% on the AV-TEST reference set; below that for 30 days and we pause new signups until fixed.

SUBSYSTEM 3

WireGuard VPN

wireguard-go client. Three VF-operated exits (Zurich, Reykjavik, Amsterdam) or bring-your-own Mullvad/IVPN config. Kill-switch enforced at the OS firewall. 24-hour iptables audit rotation, 30-minute conntrack timeout, annual third-party audit, warrant canary refreshed every 30 days.

SUBSYSTEM 4

DNS + URL filter

System-wide blocklist matching at the OS resolver: NEDNSSettings on iOS, PrivateDnsSettings on Android, NEDNSProxyProvider on macOS, systemd-resolved on Linux, DoH on Windows. Blocklist rebuilt daily from OpenPhish, AbuseCH URLhaus, Steven Black hosts, Quad9 policy replication.

SUBSYSTEM 5

Breach watch (zero-knowledge)

The client hashes your password locally; only the first 5 characters travel. Our relay strips IPs and batches lookups before hitting Have I Been Pwned. HIBP sees us; never you. Neither party can identify who is checking what.

THE PERMANENCE GUARANTEE

If VF ever exits,
your shield stays yours.

Norton was acquired into Gen Digital. Kaspersky got banned in 13 jurisdictions. Avast was fined $16.5M for selling browsing history. LastPass users watched their vaults get breached with no jurisdictional recourse. Each of those incumbents has, at some point, exited, been acquired away from its trust posture, or been documented harming its users. Guardian Shield's answer is a contractually-enforceable Permanence Guarantee.

Source · released within 90 days.

If VF Empire ever discontinues Guardian Shield, VF releases the full source code (Rust core, all three clients, all four backend services, CI + build toolchain) under a permissive open-source licence within 90 days. Escrowed in Malta + Ireland, insurance-funded execution.

Enforceable via Terms § 8 in Malta courts
Transparency log · verifiable forever.

Every signed pack + firmware release entered in a public Merkle-tree log. Verification keys mirrored to Software Heritage + Wayback Machine. A signature Guardian Shield produced in 2029 will still verify in 2049, even if VF no longer exists.

Public keys at transparency.vfempire.com/keys
Vault format · readable always.

The sealed vault format is a public spec at vf-privacy-kit/docs/vault-format.md. The reference decryption implementation is open-source. Every version ships an "Export vault" lane. Your passwords are never locked into a format only Guardian Shield can read.

Reference code at github.com/vfempire-hq/vf-privacy-kit
Signed packs · 6-month runway.

If Guardian Shield ends, the pack-distributor stays online for six months post-announcement; signed daily updates continue, giving every licence-holder time to migrate to another suite or take over pack production under the released source. Insurance-funded.

Runway underwritten by Lloyd's-syndicated policy
